To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Rb and DCC tumour suppressor gene loci were lost in two patients, the Wilms' tumour gene in three patients, and that no microsatellite mutations were detected in the 48 patients.
we did not find evidence for microsatellites or consistent LOH at selected loci.
the Rb and Wilms tumour genes, as well as the DCC gene, are unlikely to contribute to the pathogenesis of blast crisis in the vast majority of patients with CML.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular genetic mechanisms of CML and its progression to blast crisis.
the molecular genetic basis of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), a clonal haematological malignancy of the myeloid lineage, characterized by a specific translocation t(9;22)(q34;q11).
the development of a novel method to determine the number of patients with a particular type of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present results do not support the notion of a single genetic pathway in the development of CML blast crisis, but rather suggest the existence of several different pathways.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of patients with CML blast crisis do not have a genetic predisposition or a genetic instability which would be responsible for progression of the chronic phase to blast crisis.
LOH and microsatellite instability are unlikely to be important events in the progression of blast crisis in the great majority of CML patients.
the majority of CML patients do not show evidence of loss of heterozygosities in their blasts.
